Interface StatelessLoginMethod

All Known Implementing Classes:
ApiKeyLoginMethod, JwtLoginMethod
public interface StatelessLoginMethod
A way to sign in each request by a credential it carries in a header (API keys, bearer JWTs), contributed as a bean by a credential module. WhoSecurity.all() and WhoSecurity.stateless() apply every such bean.

A request that carries the credential is signed in by it or refused, so it needs no CSRF token: a browser cannot attach the header to a forged cross-site request.

    • configure

      void configure(org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.builders.HttpSecurity http)
      Adds this login method to the chain.
      Parameters:
      http - the chain being built

    • carriesCredential

      org.springframework.security.web.util.matcher.RequestMatcher carriesCredential()
      Matches the requests that carry this method's credential. Such requests are exempt from CSRF protection, so the matcher must match only when the credential is really there: a blank header must not match. Nor may a request already signed in, such as by a session cookie: its credential would not be what signs it in, so the cookie would ride along without a CSRF token.
      Returns:
      the matcher

    • presentsCredential

      default org.springframework.security.web.util.matcher.RequestMatcher presentsCredential()
      Matches the requests that present this method's credential at all, whether or not it signs them in: such a request is never treated as a browser session, even when a session cookie comes with it, so it may not do what only a browser may. By default the same as carriesCredential(); a method that ignores its credential on a request already signed in matches here regardless.
      Returns:
      the matcher

    • alreadySignedIn

      static boolean alreadySignedIn()
      Whether the current request is already signed in, by a session or anything else, before a stateless method looks at its credential: the security context holds an authentication that is not anonymous. A carriesCredential() matcher answers false then.
      Returns:
      whether the request is signed in already

    • challenge

      default Optional<String> challenge()
      The authentication scheme a signed-out 401 names in its WWW-Authenticate header, so a client learns how to sign in (RFC 9110, section 11.6.1), such as Bearer (RFC 6750). The value is written as the header's value, verbatim, once even when several methods name it. Empty for a method with no standard scheme, which adds no header.
      Returns:
      the scheme, or empty

    • name

      default String name()
      Returns this method's name, for the line who logs at startup naming the sign-in methods a chain accepts. who's own methods return a short name such as api-key.
      Returns:
      the name; by default the class's simple name, or for an anonymous class or a lambda a name built from its enclosing class
